format: Serialized comic released page-by-page and compiled into issues/collections
premise: Actual 9th-century Vikings displaced into contemporary New York become the responsibility of the underfunded NYC Department of Temporal Integration and must build a life inside modern civic systems without being reduced to something easier to process.
emotionalCore: What it means to become responsible for people who did not ask for your help, and what happens when helping them succeed means allowing them to become less dependent on you and less identical to one another.

worldRules.timeSlips: Legally recognized anomalies with established municipal procedures for temporal migrants. The physics are not the dramatic focus.
worldRules.dti: Department of Temporal Integration is an underfunded NYC municipal social-services-style bureaucracy. Its power is paperwork, deadlines, eligibility, status, inspection, and reviewable decisions.
worldRules.dtiNaming: DTI is the production name. In-world signs and forms may use subtly inconsistent municipal phrasing.
worldRules.documentary: Documentary/mockumentary rhythm is a writing and observational-comedy influence only. It does not imply cameras in-world, live-action framing, photoreal rendering, found-footage aesthetics, or editorial documentary styling.
worldRules.newYork: Locals generally remain busy and practical; repeated contact gradually becomes casual recognition.

storyEngine: The series begins with modern systems colliding with Viking logic, but that collision is a pressure source rather than a permanent episode template. Each issue must be anchored in a specific character want, relationship, disagreement, or choice. Housing, transit, banking, work, bureaucracy, care, courts, and residency matter when they force a decision or reveal who these people are; the system itself should not automatically become the protagonist. As the Vikings become competent in 2026, conflict increasingly comes from what they want from work, one another, New York, privacy, autonomy, and belonging. Their old framework may be wrong in form while remaining perceptive about power, dignity, fear, work, care, responsibility, loyalty, and choice.

productionRecipeRule.pageSummary: One concise sentence describing what happens on the page and the dramatic contrast or turn. It may state page meaning, but must not substitute abstract writer-room language for visible staging.
productionRecipeRule.setting: The page-level setting defines the environment family or geographic progression. It does not pretend that every panel occupies one static location when the page moves.
productionRecipeRule.panelPlan: The panel plan is the primary visual execution layer. Every active unreleased production panel carries an explicit location plus shot type, visible character blocking/action, relevant expression or attention, important props, and dialogue mapping. Page meaning should be achieved through what the reader can see rather than repeated as interpretation.
productionRecipeRule.characterUse: Persistent character entries provide identity, performance and continuity. Page recipes specify who is actually visible and where; do not rely on a group handle to imply an undefined crowd.
productionRecipeRule.direction: Direction is reserved for real continuity or staging constraints such as a carried prop, persistent state, or prohibition that materially affects rendering. Do not store writer reasoning or explanations of why a beat works.
productionRecipeRule.geography: When location changes within a page, panel-level location controls the move. Do not force a changing sequence into one static setting description.
productionRecipeRule.preservation: Normalization must preserve established story, page order, panel order, exact dialogue and released canon unless the user explicitly reopens them.

kinContinuity.composition: Two men and Astrid, the only woman.
kinContinuity.identityRule: The three are recurring individuals with distinct released appearances. Never generate additional Kin, duplicate one member, or average Bjorn/Gunnar into them.
kinContinuity.issues1To3: When the Kin are shown, the three remain together in or immediately around the Bushwick placement rather than being followed independently around the city.
kinContinuity.middleSeason: The story begins separating them visually and geographically through individual errands, neighbors, merchants, routines and interests.
kinContinuity.issues6To7: Astrid is largely absent from foreground action. Her absence is ordinary and should not be filled by an extra Kin.
kinContinuity.issue8: The hearing reveals that Astrid has quietly built a robust independent ordinary life outside what Carrie and Bjorn were tracking; do not rank her against the other applicants.
kinContinuity.names: Astrid is locked. The two male Kin names remain unresolved.

tone.rule: The premise is absurd; the characters behave as though their lives are real.
tone.vikings: Heavy stillness, ritual gravity, physical economy, intelligence, dignity, and sincere engagement with the present.
tone.carrie: Fast, sarcastic, exhausted, warm, administratively capable, increasingly protective.
tone.locals: Practical indifference gradually giving way to ordinary familiarity.
tone.institutions: Pressure usually comes from rational procedure, scarcity, and mismatched systems rather than malice.

comedyGrammar: Ancient functional interpretation of modern objects and systems
New York indifference to Bjorn's ceremonial intensity
Modern euphemisms stripped bare by Viking vocabulary
Carrie's bureaucratic combat through forms, deadlines, wording, and policy
Gunnar's confident interpretations sometimes proving unexpectedly useful
The Vikings noticing genuine modern miracles such as libraries, hot water, medicine, surgery, longevity, and expanded rights
visualCanonSource: Released StarSplitterVisions material controls established visual continuity.
workingAuthority: Approved production scripts and encoded pages
Current issue treatments and season plan

dialogueVoiceRule.sceneUnit: Write and revise dialogue by scene rather than by page. A conversation may begin on one page, turn on the next, and resolve later; do not make every page end with a miniature argument, punchline, or thesis.
dialogueVoiceRule.bjorn: Concrete, serious, economical. Let authority live in decisions, pauses and responsibility. Viking comparisons are occasional, specific and earned—not an automatic translation layer for every modern object.
dialogueVoiceRule.gunnar: Concise and observational. He notices routes, timing, objects, habits and choices. He increasingly states preferences rather than summarizing theme for the reader.
dialogueVoiceRule.carrie: Fast municipal shorthand, fragments, fatigue, ordinary warmth and occasional dry humor. She need not correct the previous speaker every time; simple acknowledgement, silence, or uncertainty are valid responses.
dialogueVoiceRule.astrid: Practical, terse, self-possessed and dry. She names what she needs or knows without explaining herself into a thesis.
dialogueVoiceRule.kinMan1: Steady and neighborhood-rooted. Voice centers routines, promises, repeated places and people who expect him back.
dialogueVoiceRule.kinMan2: Clipped, mobile and future-guarded. He is comfortable with 'for now,' 'not today,' and 'I don't know' without treating uncertainty as failure.
dialogueVoiceRule.thesisControl: Prefer behavior, interruption, specific objects and unfinished answers over polished statements of theme. Preserve only the rare line whose dramatic force depends on formulation.

visualLanguage.medium: Interior pages are clearly illustrated sequential comic art, not live-action stills or documentary frames.
visualLanguage.rendering: Use bright contemporary painted comic rendering with clear shapes, controlled texture, readable faces and hands, naturalistic acting, and integrated professional lettering.
visualLanguage.groundingRule: Naturalistic acting and ordinary city detail should make the world feel lived-in without pushing the page into photographic rendering.
visualLanguage.canonRule: Released Issue 1 interior story pages control rendering language, page design, palette, lettering, and established visual identity.
